source.title: SageMath De Bruijn sequences, is_debruijn_sequence(seq,k,n)
source.claim: Cyclic binary word of length 2^n with every possible n-bit substring occurring exactly once

source.title: De Bruijn sequences and universal cycles
source.claim: Binary order-n universal cycle covers 2^n windows; LFSR, Eulerian and necklace constructions are alternative algorithms, not distinct observable predicate semantics

candidate.law: For n>=1, return D1 TRUE=1 iff length(word)=2^n AND the cyclic windows word[i],...,word[(i+n-1) mod 2^n] over all starts i∈[0,2^n) are pairwise distinct (equivalently cover all 2^n possible n-bit strings exactly once). Return D1 FALSE=0 for any well-typed word failing length or uniqueness. Invalid non-D1 data or n<=0 is a domain error, never a sneaky TRUE.

witnesses.why: changed bit creates duplicate cyclic n-window
extra delimiter/bit changes required exact length
empty word never has required length
primitive 01 repetition does not cover all 2-bit patterns

falsifiers: Counting only linear substrings without wrap-around rejects valid 0011 at n=2
Accepting length 2^n with duplicate n-bit windows mistakes length for universal coverage
Treating a repeated primitive block as sufficient wrongly accepts 0101 at n=2
Treating word rotations as semantically different wrongly rejects 10001011 at n=3
Using an LFSR period alone without the all-zero state can miss one n-bit window
candidate.observable_independence: Independent of choice of Eulerian/LFSR/Lyndon algorithm to produce a cycle. Distinct predicate from selected Gray ENCODE/DECODE, PRIMITIVE-BINARY-WORD-ROOT and D8 ROTATE, but is expressible as a library over D1 bits, exact indexing and set membership; owner decides named Core resident versus selfhost library.
use_cases: SDR/radio exhaustive test frames with cyclic boundary
SENS D1 word corpus and compiler fuzz test

validation.donor_runtime: Chez Scheme R6RS exact bit windows
validation.reference_3: independent generated FKM de Bruijn witness, plus adversarial bit flips
